title: Portable handoff, stages 2 and 3: forced recovery, reconcile, and publication while active
outcome: Deferred until stage 1 is in use and a host was lost without a release, or the release-time export is too slow or too large. Then: a host that died without releasing can be replaced by an attributed takeover that a still-running old host detects within a stated window, two lineages can be reconciled without dropping either, and an active writer can publish a closed export on a cadence.
acceptance: `engram portable recover` takes over a head that is still `active` with an attributed statement, advancing the epoch by conditional advance, and is allowed only when the existing active writer's effective maximum validation age is 60 seconds or less; the changeset that adds it lowers the default age to 60 seconds, and a new default alone is not enough: against a writer whose persisted policy still says 24 hours, or a stage 1 host holding a validation taken under the longer age, `recover` is refused until an explicit transition has established the shorter bound for that writer; tests cover the persisted 24-hour policy, a custom longer age, and the old host with an old validation

A test with two simulated hosts shows that after a forced takeover the old host admits no new mutation later than 60 seconds after the takeover, and reports separately how long a write admitted before that takes to finish

Import of a payload from an active writer turns each live claim into a recoverable one through an attributed, audited event without rewriting any stored record, and a test shows the new host cannot use a claim of the old one

`engram portable reconcile` previews both lineages and continues one while keeping the other as a recovery bundle or proposed import, or forks a new project identity; it never drops a lineage or renumbers a dense feed, and tests cover each outcome

Publication while active pushes a closed export from an active writer on a cadence without freezing it, every such export already excludes the rows stage 1 excludes, and status reports the remote head and the lag; whether transfer sends only what changed is measured and stated, not assumed
